objects.description: A thin convenience wrapper around std::basic_string<char> that adds utility methods for substringing, case conversion, searching, splitting, numeric parsing, partitioning, and conversions to Unicode (String). It is value-type and follows std::string semantics.

Unicode string class built on std::basic_string<char32_t>. Adds helpers for substringing, searching, splitting, numeric parsing, partitioning, and conversions to/from ByteString (UTF-8/ASCII). Value-type semantics like std::u32string.

Exception type thrown on UTF-8 conversion failures by ByteString::FromUtf8/String::ToUtf8 implementations. Builds a message either from offending byte range or from direction flag. The helper formatError is declared here and defined elsewhere.

A small formatting builder for ByteString, similar to ostringstream but specialized. Accumulates characters in an internal buffer with basic formatting controls (flags, fill, width, precision). Provides operator<< overloads (declared below) and Build() to produce a ByteString.
A formatting builder for String (char32_t). Mirrors ByteStringBuilder but produces String. Supports operator<< overloads and Build() to obtain the final String.
Enumeration of iteration directions used by Rect iteration ranges to specify traversal order along axes.

No custom data types are defined in this header. The header only defines two constexpr floating-point constants: TPT_PI_FLT and TPT_PI_DBL. There are no structs, enums, typedefs, or classes to extract.

A small random number generator class maintaining a 128-bit internal state (two uint64_t values). It exposes utilities to generate unsigned integers, bounded integers, boolean chances, and uniform floats in [0,1). It supports seeding and getting/setting the full internal State. The exact algorithm is not documented here but appears to be a custom PRNG with a private next() step. Use dedicated instances for non-interface code; a global instance interfaceRng is declared elsewhere.
Alias for the PRNG state container: a fixed-size array of two 64-bit unsigned integers representing the 128-bit internal state of RNG. Used for saving/restoring RNG state via getters/setters.

functions.name: rasterizeLineZW
functions.signature:
template<bool Ortho, typename F>
void rasterizeLineZW(int dz, int dw, F f)
functions.description: Rasterize a discrete line from the origin on the ZW plane using a Bresenham-style algorithm, assuming abs(dw) <= dz. Iterates z from 0 to dz and invokes the callback for each rasterized (z, w). If Ortho is true, produces an orthogonally connected path by emitting the additional (z, w) step when w changes. Intended for internal use by higher-level line rasterization, but can be used directly when mapping Z and W to user axes.
requirements: dz must be a non-negative integer (the loop iterates z = 0..dz).
Precondition: abs(dw) <= dz (as documented).
The callback f must be callable as f(int z, int w).
Behavior depends on the Ortho template parameter: when true, f may be called twice for the same z when w increments.
The function does not perform bounds checking; callers mapping (z,w) to other coordinate systems must ensure resulting coordinates are valid for their domain.

template<bool Ortho, typename F>
void RasterizeLine(Vec2<int> p1, Vec2<int> p2, F f)
functions.description: Rasterize a line segment between two integer points p1 and p2 and invoke f for every point on the rasterized path. Chooses the dominant axis (X or Y) and maps to the internal ZW rasterizer. If Ortho is true, ensures orthogonal (4-connected) connectivity along the rasterized line, potentially emitting extra points on steps where the minor axis changes.
requirements: The callback f must be callable as f(Vec2<int> point).
p1 and p2 are integer coordinates; no further constraints, but very large values may risk intermediate arithmetic overflow when adding deltas.
The function may invoke f multiple times at the same coordinate if Ortho is true and the mapped increments produce duplicates; callers should tolerate possible repeats if they rely on uniqueness.

functions.name: rasterizeEllipseQuadrant
functions.signature:
template<typename F>
void rasterizeEllipseQuadrant(Vec2<float> radiusSquared, F f)
functions.description: Scan-convert the lower-right quadrant (x >= 0, y >= 0) of an axis-aligned ellipse centered at the origin whose squared radii are given by radiusSquared = (rx^2, ry^2). For each row y in [0, floor(sqrt(ry^2))], computes the inclusive horizontal interval [x1, x2] on the ellipse boundary and invokes f(x1, x2, y). Intended as a building block for full-ellipse rasterization.
requirements: radiusSquared.X (rx^2) and radiusSquared.Y (ry^2) should be finite and >= 0 for correct behavior (used with sqrt and floor).
The callback f must be callable as f(int x1, int x2, int y), where 0 <= x1 <= x2 and y >= 0.
Coordinates are computed using integer arithmetic from floating inputs; callers should expect integer truncation effects at the boundary.
If rx == 0 (radiusSquared.X == 0), the algorithm may temporarily test y > ry during boundary checks; the emitted [x1,x2] still respects ellipse constraints as implemented.

functions.signature:
template<typename F>
void RasterizeEllipsePoints(Vec2<float> radiusSquared, F f)
functions.description: Rasterize all integer points along the boundary of an axis-aligned ellipse centered at the origin with squared radii radiusSquared. Uses quadrant symmetry to emit points in up to four symmetric positions for each boundary x in the first quadrant, avoiding duplicates on axes.
requirements: radiusSquared.X and radiusSquared.Y should be finite and >= 0 (used by sqrt in the underlying quadrant routine).
The callback f must be callable as f(Vec2<int> point).
Emits each symmetric point once; no point is emitted twice on the axes (x==0 or y==0).
Only boundary points are emitted; interior points are not included.

void RasterizeEllipseRows(Vec2<float> radiusSquared, F f)
functions.description: Rasterize interior rows of an axis-aligned ellipse centered at the origin with squared radii radiusSquared. For each y in the first quadrant, computes the maximum x inside the ellipse and invokes f(xLim, y). Also mirrors to negative y (excluding y==0) to cover both top and bottom halves; callers typically fill the span [-xLim, xLim] for each y.
requirements: radiusSquared.X and radiusSquared.Y should be finite and >= 0 (used by sqrt in the underlying quadrant routine).
The callback f must be callable as f(int xLim, int y) where xLim >= 0 and y may be positive, negative, or zero depending on the call.
Only the end-of-row extent xLim is provided; callers are responsible for iterating x in [-xLim, xLim] if they wish to fill rows.

void RasterizeRect(Rect<int> rect, F f)
functions.description: Invoke f for every integer point on the boundary (perimeter) of the axis-aligned rectangle defined by rect.pos (top-left) and rect.size (width,height). Corners are emitted once; the function handles the degenerate cases where width==1 or height==1 by not double-emitting shared edges.
requirements: rect.size.X (width) and rect.size.Y (height) should be positive integers for a visible perimeter; zero or negative sizes result in empty loops or undefined region semantics.
The callback f must be callable as f(Vec2<int> point).
Coordinates are computed as [pos.X, pos.X + size.X) for x and [pos.Y, pos.Y + size.Y) for y; callers must ensure these ranges are valid for their target surface.
Very large coordinates may overflow when adding pos and size in int arithmetic; callers should avoid values that overflow int.

The parity of the dotted pattern on bottom and right edges is adjusted so corners are not double-emitted, producing a consistent dotted outline.

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator targets stubs that consume numbers and UTF-8-like strings.
# It emits a compact binary container with multiple typed fields in a fixed order
# so FUZZ_PARAM(...) and FUZZ_PARAM_STR() see interesting, valid values.
# Layout (little-endian):
#   - 8 bytes:   unsigned long long (u)
#   - 8 bytes:   signed long long (si)
#   - 8 bytes:   double (fp)
#   - 4 bytes:   unsigned int (width_src)
#   - 4 bytes:   unsigned int (prec_src)
#   - 4 bytes:   unsigned int (raw)
#   - 4 bytes:   unsigned int (which selector and other uses)
#   - 4 bytes:   unsigned int (char seeds)
#   - 4 bytes:   int (i for String::Build and StringBuilder::Add)
#   - 4 bytes:   unsigned int (cp32 for StringBuilder::Add and operator+ case 8)
#   - var bytes: sbuf for FUZZ_PARAM_STR (operator+ / == / != use)
#   - var bytes: u8   for FUZZ_PARAM_STR converted into u32 in stubs
# Strings are encoded as: 2 bytes length (0..512) followed by that many bytes.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

ASCII_SETS: List[bytes] = [
    b"",  # empty string path
    b"0", b"-1", b"+1", b"42", b"-2147483648", b"2147483647",
    b"0xDEADBEEF", b"0755", b"3.1415926535", b"-0.0", b"1e10", b"-2.5e-3",
    b"hello", b"WORLD", b"MiXeD CaSe", b"   spaced   ", b"tab\tsep", b"line\nend",
    b"hex: cafebabe", b"oct: 0777", b"scientific: 6.02e23",
]

# Some UTF-8 sequences including multibyte code points and edge cases.
UTF8_SETS: List[bytes] = [
    b"", b"\x00", b"ascii text", b"\xc2\xa9",            # ©
    b"\xe2\x82\xac",                                      # €
    b"\xf0\x9f\x98\x80",                                # 😀
    b"multi \xe6\x97\xa5\xe6\x9c\xac",                 # 日本 (partial) 
    b"mix ASCII and \xf0\x9f\x8d\x95 pizza",             # 🍕
    b"\xed\x9f\xbf\xee\x80\x80",                      # edge UTF-16 surrogate range if treated as UTF-8-like bytes
]


def _rand_bool(r: random.Random) -> bool:
    return r.getrandbits(1) == 1


def _biased_uint(r: random.Random, bits: int = 32) -> int:
    # Return unsigned with bias towards small, boundary, and random large values
    choices = []
    maxv = (1 << bits) - 1
    edges = [0, 1, 2, 7, 8, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64, 127, 128, 255, 256, 1023, 4096, 0xFFFFFFFF & maxv]
    choices.extend(edges)
    choices.append(r.randrange(0, maxv + 1))
    choices.append(r.randrange(0, maxv + 1))
    return choices[r.randrange(0, len(choices))] & maxv


def _biased_sll(r: random.Random) -> int:
    # Signed long long with boundaries
    edges = [
        0, 1, -1, 2, -2, 7, -7, 8, -8, 127, -127, 128, -128,
        255, -255, 256, -256, 1023, -1023,
        -(1 << 31), (1 << 31) - 1,
        -(1 << 63) + 1, (1 << 63) - 1,
    ]
    if _rand_bool(r):
        return r.randint(-(1 << 63) + 1, (1 << 63) - 1)
    return edges[r.randrange(0, len(edges))]


def _biased_ull(r: random.Random) -> int:
    edges = [0, 1, 2, 8, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64, 255, 256, 1023, 4095, 2**32-1, 2**48, 2**63, 2**64 - 1]
    if _rand_bool(r):
        return r.getrandbits(64)
    return edges[r.randrange(0, len(edges))] & ((1 << 64) - 1)


def _biased_double(r: random.Random) -> float:
    # Mix normals and edge cases
    special = [0.0, -0.0, 1.0, -1.0, 3.141592653589793, 2.718281828459045, 1e-308, 1e-300, 1e-10, 1e10, 1e300]
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        return special[r.randrange(0, len(special))]
    # Random normal float
    m = r.uniform(-1.0, 1.0)
    e = r.randint(-300, 300)
    return m * (10.0 ** e)


def _make_len(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> int:
    # Geometric-ish: short strings frequent, sometimes longer up to max_len
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        return r.randint(0, min(32, max_len))
    return r.randint(0, max_len)


def _rand_bytes_from_sets(r: random.Random, sets: List[bytes], fallback_max: int) -> bytes:
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        return sets[r.randrange(0, len(sets))]
    # Build random content: mix printable, whitespace, and arbitrary bytes
    length = _make_len(r, min(512, fallback_max))
    buf = bytearray()
    for _ in range(length):
        pick = r.random()
        if pick < 0.6:
            # printable ASCII
            buf.append(r.randrange(32, 127))
        elif pick < 0.8:
            # whitespace/control
            buf.append(r.choice([9, 10, 13, 32]))
        else:
            # arbitrary byte
            buf.append(r.randrange(0, 256))
    return bytes(buf)

    return struct.pack('<' + fmt, *vals)


def _len16_prefixed(b: bytes) -> bytes:
    # 2-byte little-endian length, clamped to 512
    ln = min(len(b), 512)
    return struct.pack('<H', ln) + b[:ln]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    u = _biased_ull(r)
    si = _biased_sll(r)
    fp = _biased_double(r)

    width_src = _biased_uint(r, 32)  # later mod 129 in harness
    prec_src = _biased_uint(r, 32)   # later mod 33
    raw = _biased_uint(r, 32)
    which_sel = _biased_uint(r, 32)
    char_seed = _biased_uint(r, 32)
    i_val = r.randint(-2**31, 2**31 - 1)
    cp32 = _biased_uint(r, 32)

    # Primary ASCII-ish buffer for operator+ / == / != paths
    sbuf = _rand_bytes_from_sets(r, ASCII_SETS, 512)
    # Secondary u8 buffer that will be widened to u32 code points in stubs
    u8 = _rand_bytes_from_sets(r, UTF8_SETS, 512)

    out = bytearray()
    out += _pack_le('Q', u)
    out += _pack_le('q', si)
    out += _pack_le('d', fp)
    out += _pack_le('I', width_src)
    out += _pack_le('I', prec_src)
    out += _pack_le('I', raw)
    out += _pack_le('I', which_sel)
    out += _pack_le('I', char_seed)
    out += _pack_le('i', i_val)
    out += _pack_le('I', cp32)

    # Append strings with 16-bit length prefix
    out += _len16_prefixed(sbuf)
    out += _len16_prefixed(u8)

    # Ensure size limit
    return bytes(out[:MAX_TOTAL])
